title: Format a list, one item per line
description: Write a function `format_items(items)` that returns every item of `items` on its own line.
examples:
print(format_items(['Python', 'Numpy', 'Pandas', 'Django', 'Flask']))
# Python
# Numpy
# Pandas
# Django
# Flask
hints: Method to consider: str.join(), the same tool used to build the earlier grid and triangle
Iterating with a for loop and print()-ing each item one at a time produces the same visual result as joining the items with '\n' in a single expression.
Return '\n'.join(items) directly - items is already a list of strings.
expected_behavior: Returns the items joined with newlines, one per line.
explanation: for item in items: print(item) and '\n'.join(items) produce identical output - join() is the loop, just expressed as a single method call instead of a print per iteration.
